sam.p: Quick question — new hire asked about two things: 1) when do HSA pre-tax deductions actually start after they enroll, and 2) if someone has an outstanding 401(k) loan when we do a payroll/vendor cutover, when does the loan offset hit/pay out? Need an answer I can give the recruiter by EOD.

maria.hr: thanks — is this for someone who starts mid-pay period or a future start date?

sam.p: mid-pay (starts next Tue), enrollment submitted today via Bravo form. payroll deadline confusion is what I'm trying to avoid.

jun.payroll: short answer — HSA pretax starts on the first payroll after enrollment clears payroll cutoff. cutoff = 17:00 PT, 2 business days before paydate. if enrollment arrives after cutoff it rolls to the following pay. partial proration can happen if they join mid-period.

jun.payroll: example: if paydate is Fri 4/12 and cutoff was Tue 4/9 17:00 PT, enroll by Tue 4/9 16:59 to hit 4/12. after that it becomes 4/26. :calendar:

priya.benefits: adding: employer HSA contributions (if applicable) follow the payroll they are tied to — so you won't see employer contribs until the first payroll that shows employee pre-tax. also remind them to confirm bank info for HSA vendor.

priya.benefits: if they enrolled via the e-sign link today, tell them to check the confirmation email — that is what we use to verify enrollment hit the vendor.

sam.p: great — what about the 401(k) loan offset during vendor cutover? recruiter is worried they'll get hit with taxes or a big gap.

drew.finance: we did this in last vendor migration. rough flow: old vendor processes loan offsets as of the transfer date. if offset is treated as a distribution, taxes may apply immediately (federal + state where applicable). new vendor receives participant balances but offsets that were processed already are reflected as a distribution on the old vendor side.

drew.finance: timeline: offsets often process within 1-2 payroll cycles of cutover depending on timing. if the participant remains employed and continues payroll deductions, repayment won't magically resume unless plan allows post-offset repayment — usually it's considered in default and becomes distribution. we can check plan doc but default behavior: offset = distribution unless a formal repayment plan is set up. :warning:

priya.benefits: important to note — if offset becomes a taxable distribution and the participant is under 59½, there may be additional early withdrawal penalties. they should get a 1099-R for that tax year.

jun.payroll: operational note — for payroll team to avoid surprises we need the employee's payroll ID to map across vendors. ask recruiter for employee number + SSN last 4 when coordinating cutover.

benefits-bot: Quick links: Plan migration checklist: https://intra.redwood/benefits/migration-checklist • HSA vendor enrollment guide: https://intra.redwood/benefits/hsa-enroll • 401k loan FAQ: https://intra.redwood/benefits/401k-loan-faq

sam.p: super helpful. will tell recruiter: enroll ASAP before cutoff to get HSA on first paycheck; 401k loan offsets may process within 1-2 pay cycles and could be treated as distribution (taxes may apply). I'll have payroll/benefits follow up re: SSN mapping. thanks all! :thumbsup:

maria.hr: tagging @jun.payroll and @priya.benefits to confirm we'll proactively flag mid-pay hires during the next two cutovers so recruiters get a short checklist.

jun.payroll: yep we can add a checklist item in the recruiter intake form — i'll draft and post in #people-ops later today.

priya.benefits: I'll add a one-line in the benefits guide about loan offsets + 1099s.

sam.p: perfect — closing this thread.
